title: SmoothStep allocator for dedicated throughput SLA matching
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem statement: For Dedicated fleets we need an autoscaling policy engine that reliably maps customer throughput commitments (per-tenant throughput contracts) to fleet capacity while minimizing oscillation and avoiding costly overprovisioning. Current step-scaling rules react to short spikes and cause thrashing on heterogeneous workloads (mixed short chat vs long-context generation). This ticket proposes the SmoothStep allocator: a quantile-aware, minimal-oscillation autoscaler that blends short and long horizons, enforces contract guarantees, and exposes explicit safety limits for fleet operators.
background_and_constraints: Constraints: fleets host multi-tenant workloads with differing token-length distributions and strict throughput SLAs (tokens/sec or queries/sec). We must preserve latency SLOs for P0 customers, avoid noisy neighbor amplification, and ensure quick rollback in case of regressions. The allocator must integrate with existing runtime metrics pipeline (token emission rate, in-flight KV cache hit rates, per-model sequence-length histogram) and Redwood's rollout primitives (canary, A/B). Budget: non-disruptive rollout, limited infra changes to runtime, leverage current autoscaler hooks.
proposed_solution_summary: Implement SmoothStep allocator as a policy layer that computes a target capacity delta every control tick based on: 1) a multi-horizon demand forecast (short 30s, medium 5m, long 30m) derived from token-rate quantiles; 2) a damped PI controller applied to the chosen quantile to avoid step changes; 3) per-tenant commitment enforcement using contract credits and min-guarantee reservations; 4) safety fences that cap scale rate, bound min/max replicas, and reserve warmup lanes for predicted bursts.
scaling_algorithm_details: quantile_selector: choose quantile q(t) = weighted_percentile(p50..p99) where weights favor higher quantiles when cache_hit_ratio < 0.7
damped_PI: delta_capacity = clamp(Kp * error + Ki * integral(error), -max_step, +max_step) with integral decay across 'medium' horizon to prevent accumulation from transient spikes
smoothstep_blend: final_delta = SmoothStep(delta_short, delta_medium, delta_long) using kernel weights (0.6, 0.3, 0.1) configurable per-fleet
demand_weighting: normalize by tenant_priority_factor and model_efficiency_score (tokens/sec per GPU), so committed throughput maps to replica counts
prefill_warmup: reserve warm_lanes tokens to pre-warm KV caches when forecast shows >20% short-horizon growth
safety_limits_and_failsafes: min_replicas: per-fleet configurable lower bound to guarantee baseline throughput
max_replicas: enforced by contract and capacity pool to cap cost exposure
max_scale_step_per_minute: default 2 replicas/min (configurable); absolute cap to avoid runaway scaling
cooldown_window_seconds: 90s by default after any scale-out event to allow runtime stabilization
rollback_trigger: if p95_latency increases >25% or error_rate >2% for 3 consecutive ticks, revert last scale action and open incident
graceful_eviction_policy: when shedding is required, evict best-effort traffic first based on tenant_priority and recent_request_success_rate
budgeted_warmup_tokens: prevent warmup allocations from exceeding a percentage of total pool (default 15%) to avoid starving steady-state capacity
api_and_config_exposure: operator flags: min_replicas, max_replicas, max_step_per_minute, cool_down, quantile_weights
observability: expose 'desired_replicas', 'applied_replicas', 'scale_decision_reason' and time-series for the quantiles used
rollout hooks: canary_percentage and evaluation_metrics (latency/regression) before full flip
acceptance_criteria: 1) Unit + integration tests for SmoothStep allocator logic with synthetic workloads covering short/medium/long burst patterns
2) E2E staging run with a copy of a production token-mix for a dedicated fleet showing <= 10% extra cost vs current baseline while meeting committed throughput in 95% of 24h windows
3) No new SLO regressions in canary traffic for two consecutive days; rollback plan verified
4) Dashboard tiles added to Console to show target vs applied capacity and the quantile inputs used in decisions
5) Runbook updated with incident steps for rollback_trigger and manual override instructions
test_and_validation_plan: synthetic load tests: ramp profiles for chat-like (many short requests) and generation-like (long sequences) with tenant-mix ratios
fault injection: delay KV cache hits and simulate noisy neighbor to validate dampening behavior
A/B canary: 10% of traffic for 48h comparing SmoothStep vs current autoscaler under the same load
cost simulation: project hourly cost under forecasted workloads and compare to historical billing for a 2-week window
deployment_and_rollout: phase 0: internal unit tests + code review (target 1 week)
phase 1: staging fleet rollout with synthetic workloads (target 2 weeks)
phase 2: low-risk canary on non-critical tenant fleets (10% traffic, 48h), monitor rollback_triggers
phase 3: gradual expansion to committed fleets with 24h gating per 25% traffic increase
operator_manual_override: api to set allocator_mode=manual and force_replicas until issue resolved
open_issues_and_risks: forecast quality: quantile forecasts rely on stable telemetry; sparse telemetries can bias quantiles upward
model_efficiency_estimates: need better telemetry to map tokens->GPU consumption for mixed architectures
cross-tenant fairness: enforced guarantees may starve best-effort tenants during capacity constraints; need policy for degraded fairness
rollback latency: reverting scale changes takes time on some hardware; plan includes prefilling warm lanes to reduce pain but more testing required
